Name: Kirchbichl
note: TIWAG Innkraftwerk Kirchbichl (run-of-river Schlingenkraftwerk): 19.3 MW before the 2017-2020 expansion, 37.9 MW bottleneck capacity incl. the 0.75 MW Dotierkraftwerk since the fourth Kaplan unit went online in October 2020 (https://www.tiwag.at/unternehmen/unsere-kraftwerke/kraftwerk/kraftwerk-kirchbichl/; https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kraftwerk_Kirchbichl); powerplantmatching carries the pre-expansion 16 MW as Reservoir

Name: St Veit St Veit
note: VERBUND Laufkraftwerk St. Veit (real capacity 17 MW)

Name: Walgauwerk
note: illwerke vkw Walgauwerk; diversion run-of-river using Rodund outflow (356 GWh/a)

Name: Enzingerboden
note: OeBB Kraftwerk Enzingerboden fed from Tauernmoossee reservoir

Name: St Pantaleon
note: Ennskraftwerk St. Pantaleon (1965) on the lower Enns near its Danube mouth (St. Pantaleon-Erla, NOe); powerplantmatching geocoded the same-named village on the Salzach in Bezirk Braunau (48.0076 N 12.8942 E) which lands the plant in AT311 on a river section without any plant; relocated to the Enns (approximate coordinates inside KLIEN section 51200) ; coordinates from https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laufkraftwerk_St._Pantaleon

Name: Bockstein
note: Salzburg AG Kraftwerk Boeckstein (Nassfelder Ache, Bad Gastein); powerplantmatching geocoded the operator address in Salzburg city (AT323); relocated to Boeckstein in the Pongau (approximate coordinates inside KLIEN section 40406)

Name: Kaprun Haupstufe
note: Verbund Kaprun Hauptstufe: 220 MW turbine capacity without pumps (https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kraftwerksgruppe_Kaprun); ppm nameplate 260 MW; KLIEN section 40303 C_current 261 MW equals the Hauptstufe only

Name: Kaprun Limberg
note: ppm merges Limberg I (113 MW turbine and pump, 1955) and Limberg III (480 MW, September 2025) into one 740 MW entry; corrected to 593 MW (https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kraftwerksgruppe_Kaprun); the second ppm entry Kaprun Limberg 480 MW is Limberg II (2011)

Name: Prutz
note: TIWAG Kraftwerk Kaunertal at Prutz: 392 MW maximum capacity (https://www.tiwag.at/uploads/tx_bh/448/tiwag_unsere_kraftwerke_kaunertal_kraftwerksbroschuere_webansicht_rz.pdf); ppm nameplate 481 MW

Name: Reisseck
note: Verbund Reisseck II (430 MW reversible, 2016) plus Reisseck II plus (45 MW, June 2025) = 475 MW (https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kraftwerksgruppe_Rei%C3%9Feck-Kreuzeck); the old Reisseck-Kreuzeck storage plants at Kolbnitz (136 MW, no pumps) are added separately as a missing plant

Name: Ausserfragant
note: KELAG Kraftwerk Ausserfragant: three Pelton units with 96 MW (https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kraftwerksgruppe_Fragant); ppm nameplate 100 MW

Name: Illwerke Vkw Rodundwerk
note: ppm merges Rodundwerk I (198 MW turbine, 41 MW pump, 1943; https://www.illwerkevkw.at/rodundwerk-i) and Rodundwerk II (295 MW, 1976; https://www.illwerkevkw.at/rodundwerk-ii); the entry is reduced to Rodundwerk I and Rodundwerk II is added as a missing pumped-storage plant

Name: Illwerke Vkw Vermuntwerk
note: illwerke vkw Vermuntwerk: 170 MW turbine capacity (https://www.illwerkevkw.at/vermuntwerk); ppm nameplate 193 MW

Name: Landl
note: Verbund Laufkraftwerk Landl on the Enns: run-of-river, 25 MW, 136 GWh/a, 1967 (https://www.verbund.com/de-at/ueber-verbund/kraftwerke/unsere-kraftwerke/landl); ppm has it as a 48 MW reservoir; the E-Control Anlagenregister lists 24 MW at Grossreifling

Name: Weyer
note: Ennskraftwerke Laufkraftwerk Weyer on the Enns at Weyer, 36.8 MW, 1969 (https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ennskraftwerke_AG); ppm geocoded it near the Traun (48.15 N 14.12 E) in AT312; relocated to the Enns at Weyer in AT314 (approximate coordinates; one of the two units feeds the OeBB 16.7 Hz railway grid with 18 MW)

Name: Altenmarkt
note: Verbund Laufkraftwerk Altenmarkt on the Enns at Altenmarkt bei St. Gallen, 26 MW, 150 GWh/a, 1960 (https://www.verbund.com/de-at/ueber-verbund/kraftwerke/unsere-kraftwerke/altenmarkt); ppm geocoded a same-named village in southern Styria (AT225); relocated to the Enns (approximate coordinates)

Name: Wald
note: Salzburg AG Speicherkraftwerk Wald: intake on the Krimmler Ache below the Krimml falls, daily storage at Oberkrimml, 4.6 km tunnel, powerhouse at Wald im Pinzgau with tailwater into the Salzach, 23.5 MW, 64 GWh/a, 1988 (https://www.salzburg-ag.at/ueber-die-salzburg-ag/unternehmen/erzeugung/erzeugungsanlagen/wasserkraftwerk-wald.html); powerplantmatching geocoded it to the operator address; the powerhouse coordinates (OSM centroid) fall into the KLIEN catchment 40100 Salzach up to Pegel Wald (C_current 29.5 MW = Wald 23.5 + Trattenbach 5.1), where the study books it

Name: Krippau
note: Verbund Laufkraftwerk Krippau on the Enns at Altenmarkt bei St. Gallen: run-of-river, 30 MW, 175 GWh/a, 1965 (https://www.verbund.com/de-at/ueber-verbund/kraftwerke/unsere-kraftwerke/krippau); ppm has it as a 60 MW reservoir

Name: Gaming
note: powerplantmatching lists 'Gaming' with 14 MW, no technology and coordinates in Vienna; the plant is Wien Energie's Wasserleitungskraftwerk Gaming I+II on the II. Wiener Hochquellenleitung at Gaming (NOe), 5.6 MW electrical, about 40 GWh/a, 1926/1990 (https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wasserleitungskraftwerk_Gaming; https://www.wienenergie.at/projekt/wasserkraft-anlagen-wien-energie/); no 14 MW plant exists at Gaming; corrected to 5.6 MW run-of-river at the true site so that the small-hydro replacement step drops it in favour of the Anlagenregister entry (without a technology the entry would silently fall out of the model)
